<description>
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.
</description>

Right. When I wrote this back in July, this was intentional, because I assumed that unclean shutdowns are rare enough to just let the user quickly create a fresh txindex. However, I think the picture has changed in the meantime:

* Ralph LLM flagged this, so other bots will likely flag and fix this when this is merged. Also, it could make Fuzzamoto/bedrock testing harder, because it can surface these rare errors.
* There are plans to support pruning while having indexes, so quickly re-creating an index may actually be tedious.

I didn't take your comment, because the code paths are also reachable when doing something fancy such as:

* Run with txindex and reorg out a block
* Drop block folder and sync again with txindex disabled
* Restart with txindex and submit the stale block header

There is probably no need to enumerate all of them in the code. Modern LLMs should be capable to enumerate them for anyone who needs them.

I think a unit test is not needed, so I'll skip it for now.

[2026-10-30] rc:4423984199 inline on src/rpc/rawtransaction.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-30):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35728#discussion_r4421983063

Not blocking, but I'm not sure the other callers are a good reason to add the race here. `getrawtransaction` didn't have it before this PR, because it only checked `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA` after the read failed. Since this call is new, it seems better to add it in a form that doesn't race, for example by re-checking when `GetTransaction` throws, as in the snippet above. That is also the direction of furszy's suggestion to have `ReadBlock` report the kind of failure.

The race case also matters a bit more here, because it reports "I/O error reading block data" for a block that was just pruned, the kind of misreport this PR is fixing. [`GetBlockChecked`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/fab96992ac470645544c21adbe48f9b5288199a1/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L725-L740) has the same pattern but reports a neutral "Block not found on disk".
